relations.note: Cain and Abel are brothers, both sons of Adam and Eve.

relations.myth: The brothers present rival offerings to YHWH
relations.note: Cain’s offering is disregarded while Abel’s offering receives divine favor.

relations.myth: Cain murders Abel in the field
relations.note: Cain rises against his brother Abel and kills him.

relations.myth: Cain presents produce as an offering
relations.note: Cain offers fruit of the ground, but YHWH does not regard it.

relations.myth: YHWH warns Cain about crouching sin
relations.note: YHWH warns the angry Cain that sin desires him and must be mastered.

relations.myth: YHWH interrogates Cain after Abel’s murder
relations.note: YHWH questions Cain and exposes Abel’s blood crying from the ground.

relations.myth: Cain is cursed and exiled
relations.note: YHWH curses Cain from the soil and condemns him to wandering.

relations.myth: YHWH grants Cain a protective sign
relations.note: YHWH protects Cain from retaliatory killing with a sign and sevenfold vengeance.
Eve conceives, bears, and names Cain with a qnh wordplay.
Adam fathers Cain after knowing Eve.
Jubilees identifies Awan as Cain’s sister.
Cain marries his sister Awan in Jubilees.
Cain fathers Enoch and names a city after him.
Cain is Irad’s genealogical ancestor through Enoch.
Cain is Mehujael’s ancestor in the Cainite genealogy.
Cain is Methushael’s ancestor in the Cainite genealogy.
Cain is Lamech’s ancestor in the Cainite genealogy.

relations.myth: Lamech invokes Cain’s sevenfold protection
relations.note: Lamech magnifies Cain’s sevenfold vengeance into a seventy-sevenfold boast.

relations.myth: Blind Lamech accidentally kills Cain
relations.note: Later legend identifies Cain as the victim accidentally shot by blind Lamech.
Cain is Jabal’s genealogical ancestor through Lamech and Adah.
Cain is Jubal’s genealogical ancestor through Lamech and Adah.
Cain is Tubal-Cain’s genealogical ancestor through Lamech and Zillah.

relations.myth: Tubal-Cain assists Lamech’s accidental shooting
relations.note: Later legend makes Tubal-Cain direct blind Lamech when Lamech accidentally kills Cain.
Cain is Naamah’s genealogical ancestor through Lamech and Zillah.

relations.myth: Seth replaces the Abel whom Cain killed
relations.note: Seth is appointed as replacement seed for Abel, Cain’s murdered brother.

relations.myth: Enoch witnesses Abel’s accusation against Cain
relations.note: Enoch encounters Abel’s spirit continuing its accusation until Cain’s lineage is destroyed.

relations.myth: Enoch sees Cain as a dark bovine
relations.note: Enoch’s animal vision represents Cain as a dark bovine killing red Abel.
The Gnostic chief ruler fathers Cain through sexual violation of Eve.

relations.myth: Yaldabaoth deceptively names his archontic offspring
relations.note: Yaldabaoth deceptively gives one of his generated rulers the name Cain.
A Gnostic recension identifies or pairs Cain with the archontic ruler Eloim.
Later Gnostic and Jewish legends make the serpent-Samael Cain’s supernatural father.
Some later legendary forms make Satan Cain’s father through Eve.

relations.myth: Satan instructs Cain how to murder
relations.note: Islamic tales sometimes have Satan demonstrate or instruct Cain in killing Abel.

relations.myth: Sophia rescues Cain’s higher spiritual element
relations.note: Reported Gnostic systems say Sophia rescues Cain’s higher element from the creator’s assault.

relations.myth: Cainite figures oppose the world-maker
relations.note: Irenaeus reports Cain and Esau grouped as spiritual kin opposing the creator.

relations.myth: Cainite figures oppose the world-maker
relations.note: Irenaeus reports Cain and Korah grouped among figures opposing the creator.

relations.myth: Cainite heresiology groups Cain with Judas
relations.note: Heresiologists associate reverence for Cain with a positive valuation of Judas.

relations.myth: Cain’s hatred contrasts with Christlike self-giving love
relations.note: Cain’s evil murder is contrasted with the self-giving love exemplified by Christ.
